title: ChangeUserRole
description: The body of an administrative role change, derived from identity_application::administration::ChangeUserRole. It carries the AdminContext, so the actor and the session they act under travel with the command rather than being inferred at the transport — which is what gives the AAL2 check somewhere to happen.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; ChangeUserRoleCommand has no body and no route serves it

context.description: Who is asking, and under which session.

user_id.description: The user whose role changes. May NOT equal context.actor_id — that is the SelfChange refusal, and it is reached before any other rule.

new_role.description: The role to assign. The CURRENT role and the ACTOR's role are not request fields: RoleChangeRequest carries them, but they are resolved by the command that builds that request, from the store, inside the transaction. A body that let a caller state the current role would let a caller lie about it.

x-not-on-the-wire.actor_role: resolved from the actor's session by the command; a caller-supplied actor_role would be a caller claiming its own authority
x-not-on-the-wire.current_role: read from the store inside the transaction
x-not-on-the-wire.target_status: read from the store inside the transaction
x-not-on-the-wire.active_administrator_count: COUNTED inside the same transaction that applies the change. This is the field the whole last-administrator rule turns on, and reading it outside the transaction is the race Phase 6's exit condition names.

x-success-response: PlatformRole — the new role. The command's return type is ApplicationResult<PlatformRole>, not the AccountView a self-service command would return, because the administrative surface is a different boundary.
